_meta.indication: DALVANCE is indicated for acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by designated susceptible strains of Gram-positive microorganisms.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multisite, double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, controlled trial comparing dalbavancin with vancomycin followed by a possible switch to oral linezolid; non-inferiority margin pre-specified at 10%.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) known or suspected to be caused by gram-positive bacteria.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response (responder: no increase from baseline in lesion area and temperature at or below 37.6°C) at 48-72 hours after initiation of therapy.
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 301 early clinical response at 48-72h: dalbavancin 240/288 (83.3%) vs vancomycin/linezolid 233/285 (81.8%); difference 1.5% (95% CI -4.6, 7.9), meeting non-inferiority at the 10% margin.

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dalbavancin for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multisite, double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, controlled trial comparing dalbavancin with vancomycin followed by a possible switch to oral linezolid; non-inferiority margin pre-specified at 10%. Sample size was increased in Trial 302 (enrolled 739 patients).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) known or suspected to be caused by gram-positive bacteria.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response (no increase from baseline in lesion area and temperature at or below 37.6°C) at 48-72 hours after initiation of therapy.
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 302 early clinical response at 48-72h: dalbavancin 285/371 (76.8%) vs vancomycin/linezolid 288/368 (78.3%); difference -1.5% (95% CI -7.4, 4.6), meeting non-inferiority at the 10% margin.

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dalbavancin for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were nausea (5.5%), headache (4.7%), and diarrhea (4.4%). ALT elevations >3x ULN were more frequent with dalbavancin; serious hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) and skin reactions have been reported with glycopeptides including DALVANCE.
target_moa: Dalbavancin is a semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide that interferes with bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of the stem pentapeptide in nascent cell wall peptidoglycan, preventing cross-linking; bactericidal in vitro against S. aureus and S. pyogenes.

rems.type: Based on available data and the potential benefits and risks, a REMS requirement could not be established; adverse reactions were addressed in labeling and monitored by routine pharmacovigilance.

advisory_committee.vote: The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (March 30, 2014) voted 12 in favor and 0 against that dalbavancin was safe and effective for treating patients with ABSSSI.

summary.text: Dalbavancin received QIDP designation for ABSSSI (October 25, 2012) and fast track designation (2003); as a QIDP product under GAIN it received a priority review and is eligible for 5 additional years of marketing exclusivity. The NDA was approved for ABSSSI based on two Phase 3 non-inferiority trials (301 and 302), not under accelerated approval.
